You build ONE clinical-test MINI-GAME plugin for Lumen. Contract: MiniGameModule in src/core/minigame.ts — read it carefully. Your folder's index.ts must `export default` the module (or an array of modules when your folder implements two TestIds). The exam room opens your game inside a large modal stage (assume ~960x620 desktop, full-screen on phones, ≥ 375px wide) and passes a MiniGameContext: patient, the patient's true PatientFindings, mode ('case' | 'practice'), difficulty 0..1, rng, audio, fx, reducedMotion.

Design rules for every mini-game:
- It must feel like operating a beautiful, precise optical INSTRUMENT: tactile dials/knobs (drag + mouse wheel + arrow keys), lens clicks (ctx.audio.play('lens-click'|'dial'|...)), smooth eased animation, glows, depth. Reuse @render (eye renderer: drawEye/EyeCanvas/eyeStateFromFindings/drawSlitSection/paintIrisArt; fundus: paintFundus/FundusView; avatars: PatientAvatar; FX) and @ui-kit components (Button, Icon, GlassPanel, Meter, etc.) — read src/render/**/index.ts and src/ui-kit/index.ts for their real APIs first.
- Layout: a slim header strip with a one-line instruction + OD/OS eye selector where relevant; the instrument stage; a footer with progress and a gold 'Record findings' button. A first-time micro-tutorial overlay (2-3 steps, skippable).
- The behaviour must be OPTICALLY/CLINICALLY TRUE to the findings (e.g. blur scales with uncorrected refractive error, a +lens fogs a myope, RAPD shows paradoxical dilation, against-motion for myopia beyond the working distance, mires overlap at the true IOP...). Use docs/research/03-test-mechanics.md for procedure and scales.
- In 'case' mode the chart must be clinically correct: call done() with findings = report(ctx.findings, ctx.patient) (true values, flagged normal/abnormal/critical vs norms), and accuracy 0..1 reflecting how well the player performed the technique (precision, completeness, time); set perfect when flawless. In 'practice' mode end with a recognition challenge (e.g. 'What is the IOP?', 'Which eye has the RAPD?', 'With or against?') and score it; show the answer with a short teaching explanation.
- report() is pure and well-unit-tested: it turns findings into crisp chart lines (e.g. label 'IOP', value '48 mmHg', eye 'OD', flag 'critical').
- practice(rng, difficulty) generates varied, clinically coherent scenarios using buildFindings + generateAvatar (from @render) — mix normal and pathological, harder with difficulty.
- Call done() exactly once; the returned cleanup must remove every listener, RAF, timer, and DOM node. Keyboard accessible, touch-friendly, honours ctx.reducedMotion. No console errors.
- View & screenshot it at ?sandbox=minigame/<id> (add &case=<caseId> to use a real case if any exist; the harness shows the result JSON after done()). Drive interactions with a throwaway Playwright script (require('playwright')) to verify the whole flow reaches done().
- Player-facing text: never any sin words.

=== YOUR MINI-GAME: visual-acuity + pinhole (export an array of TWO modules: ids 'visual-acuity' and 'pinhole') — folder src/minigames/visual-acuity/ ===
A gorgeous back-lit projector chart (Snellen letters in proper Sloan optotype proportions, plus a LogMAR/ETDRS mode toggle; tumbling-E or LEA symbols for young children). The chart is blurred realistically according to the eye's uncorrected refractive error (blur from spherical equivalent and cylinder — astigmatism blurs directionally) and pathology (BCVA limit). Player occludes one eye (animated occluder on a mini patient avatar), points to lines, and the patient 'reads' via speech bubbles — reading correctly above threshold and making characteristic errors near it; the player must find the smallest line read (≥ more than half the letters) for OD, OS, (OU optional). Accuracy = how close the recorded acuity is to truth & technique (occluding correctly, one eye at a time). Record logMAR and Snellen (respect metric VA setting is not available in ctx — show 20/x with 6/x secondary). PINHOLE module: the occluder flips to a pinhole; refractive blur clears and pathology does not — player judges 'improves' vs 'no improvement'. report(): VA sc OD/OS, PH if relevant; flag abnormal when worse than 20/40 (critical at ≤ 20/200).

=== YOUR MINI-GAME: phoropter — folder src/minigames/phoropter/ ===
Subjective refraction on a stunning brass-and-glass phoropter (front view with the two lens apertures, dials for sphere, cylinder, axis, JCC flip, duochrome toggle). The patient view chart blurs per the residual refractive error: residual = true Rx − dialled lens (vector math for cylinder; use power vectors M, J0, J45). Classic flow: start from a retinoscopy/autorefraction estimate (perturbed by difficulty), fog, sphere bracketing with 'which is better, one or two?' prompts the PATIENT answers (truthfully with occasional uncertainty near endpoint), JCC axis then power refinement, maximum plus to best VA, duochrome check, optional binocular balance. Patient answers come in speech bubbles. Accuracy from final Rx error (spherical equivalent and cylinder vector distance; quarter-dioptre precision) and number of steps. report(): Rx OD/OS in minus-cyl formatted with formatRx, BCVA, Add if presbyopic; flag abnormal when significantly ametropic? (flag 'normal' for any correctable refraction unless BCVA reduced).

=== YOUR MINI-GAME: retinoscopy — folder src/minigames/retinoscopy/ ===
Streak retinoscopy: the player sweeps a streak (mouse/touch drag or arrow keys) across a big glowing pupil with a red-orange reflex. The reflex moves WITH (hyperopic/under-plussed relative to working distance) or AGAINST (myopic beyond far point), speed and brightness and width vary with how far from neutral; at neutrality the pupil fills/flashes. Player rotates the streak to find principal meridians (astigmatism: the reflex is broken/misaligned off-axis; band aligns at the correct axis), adds lenses from a lens rack / dial to neutralise each meridian, and remembers working distance (e.g. 67cm → subtract +1.50 D). Reflex quality per findings.retinoscopyReflex: 'scissors' (keratoconus), 'dull' (cataract/media opacity), 'absent'. Accuracy from final net Rx vs truth. report(): 'Ret' net result per eye + reflex quality flags.

=== YOUR MINI-GAME: keratometry — folder src/minigames/keratometry/ ===
Keratometer (one-position Bausch & Lomb style): view through the eyepiece shows the three mires on the cornea; the player focuses (doubling → single), aligns horizontal and vertical plus/minus signs by turning two measurement drums, and rotates the instrument to the principal meridian. Reading K1/K2 and axis; irregular/distorted mires for keratoconus. Show the corneal cylinder = K difference. Accuracy from reading error. report(): K1/K2 @ axis per eye, corneal astigmatism, mires quality; flag abnormal for steep K > 47 D or irregular mires.

=== YOUR MINI-GAME: pupils — folder src/minigames/pupils/ ===
Pupil exam in a dimmed room: big close-up of BOTH eyes (use @render eye renderer, lighting 'dim'/'penlight') with a penlight the player controls (drag, or keys to swing). Pupils constrict/dilate with realistic latency and dynamics; consensual response; swinging flashlight test where an RAPD eye paradoxically dilates when the light swings onto it (grade by findings.pupils.rapdGrade); anisocoria that differs in light vs dark (Horner: small pupil worse in dark + mild ptosis; CN3/Adie: large pupil worse in light; Adie tonic slow redilation; light-near dissociation via a near-target button). Measure pupil sizes with a pupil gauge overlay (half-circles 2-9mm). Player tasks: measure sizes in light and dark, perform swinging light ≥ 3 swings, test near. Accuracy: technique (dwell time 2-3s per eye, enough swings) + measurement accuracy. report(): sizes light/dark, reactivity, RAPD (critical), near response, anisocoria.

=== YOUR MINI-GAME: cover-test — folder src/minigames/cover-test/ ===
Cover/uncover and alternate cover test on a close-up of the patient's eyes (@render eye renderer, gaze offsets) with a translucent black occluder paddle the player moves (drag/keys) between eyes, distance vs near target toggle. Simulate exactly: tropia — covering the fixating eye makes the deviated eye take up fixation (refixation movement in the correct direction: eso → moves out; exo → moves in; hyper → down); phoria — no movement on cover; on uncover the covered eye recovers; alternate cover reveals total deviation. Then a prism bar the player slides in (base-out for eso, base-in for exo) until neutralised to measure prism dioptres. Accuracy from correct classification (ortho/phoria/tropia/intermittent, eso/exo/hyper, which eye) + prism measurement. report(): distance & near deviation e.g. '12Δ constant L esotropia' with flags.

=== YOUR MINI-GAME: motility + convergence (export an array of TWO modules: 'motility' and 'convergence') — folder src/minigames/motility/ ===
MOTILITY: broad H-pattern — the player moves a glowing fixation wand (drag/keys) through the 9 positions of gaze while the patient's eyes (@render eye renderer or high-quality SVG of both eyes on the avatar face) follow; versions per findings.motility.versions show underactions/overactions (e.g. CN6: abduction deficit; CN4: affected eye overelevates in adduction; CN3: eye down-and-out with ptosis); patient reports diplopia in certain gazes and pain on movement (optic neuritis). Player marks the motility diagram (H chart with +/- grades) — accuracy from correct grading. CONVERGENCE: an RAF accommodative target moves towards the nose along a ruler; eyes converge until the break point (findings.motility.npcCm) when one eye drifts out and the patient says 'double!'; player stops the target at break and recovery; also amplitude of accommodation push-up (blur point vs expected for age). report(): versions summary, NPC break/recovery cm (abnormal > 10cm), amplitude.
